sentences.text: Rhinosteus was a small to medium-sized placoderm, an extinct armored fish, featuring short cheeks and slender lower jaw plates.
The species R. traquairi and R. tuberculatus possessed long, pointed rostrums and tubercles on their plates, with the rostrum in R. traquairi extending sharply beyond the snout.
The average skull length of R. tuberculatus is 15 centimetres, whereas R. parvulus measures only 4 to 6 centimetres.
The genus Rhinosteus was described by Jaekel in 1911, with three species known: the type species R. traquairi, and R. parvulus and R. tuberculatus described by Gross in 1932.
Rhinosteus is classified as a member of the class Placodermi and belongs to the family Selenosteidae within the clade Aspinothoracidi, which is part of the major clade Pachyosteomorphi.
Rhinosteus lived during the Frasnian stage, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago, with fossils found in the Upper Frasnian Kellwasserkalk facies in Germany and Morocco.
